div.l: The feyth is this the kut fell on the knight
Of which full glad was eủery wight
And telle he most his tale as it was resoıı̄un
By foreward and by composicoıı̄un
As ye haue herde what nedeth wordes mo
And whan this gode man saw þat it was so
As he þat wyse was and obedient
To kepe his foreward by his free assent
And seide setth I shall begynne the game
Wele come be þe cut in goddes name
Now late vs ryde and herkeneth what I sey
And wᵗith þᵗat worde we ryden̄ forth our wey
And he began wᵗith right a mery chere
This tale anone and seide on þis man̉ere
Iamqꝫue domos patrias scithice post asꝑpera gentis prelia laurigero
Here begynneth the knightes tale
Whilom þere was as old stories tellen vs
A duke a worthy man þat hight Theseus
Of Athenes he was lord and goủernour
And in his tyme swich a conquerour
That gretter Was there none vndre þe sonne
Full many a riches contre hade he Wonne
What with his Wysdome and chiualrye
He conquered aƚƚ the reigne of Femenye
That whilom̄ cleped was Scitha
And wedded þe fressh quene ypolita
And brought hir home wᵗith hym to his contre
Wᵗith moch glorie and grete solempnite
And eke hir yonge suster Emelye
And þus with blis and wᵗith victorye
Lete I this noble duk to Attene ryde
And all his oft in armes by his syde
And certes yf it ne Were to long to here
I wold haue told fully the manere
How wonne Was þe reigne of Femenye
By Theseus and by his chiualrye
And of þe grete bataill for the nones
Bitwene the Atthenes and Amasones
